title: Iran war: Trump sought allied help, then said 'WE NEVER DID' need it

before.quote: Many countries ... will be sending warships ... to keep the Strait of Hormuz open and safe.
before.where: Truth Social statement calling for international assistance securing the Strait of Hormuz

after.quote: We no longer 'need,' or desire, the NATO Countries' assistance — WE NEVER DID!
after.where: Truth Social post after NATO allies declined to join the operation

context: During the March 2026 Iran war, Trump publicly called for other countries to help protect shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. After NATO allies declined involvement, he claimed the United States never needed their help. On March 17 he also said in the Oval Office, 'we don't need them, but they should have been there.' This is a documented reversal in his public description of whether allied help was needed; asking for help and later saying it was not strictly necessary are not inherently logically incompatible. Sources: https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/trump-says-natos-refusal-to-help-on-iran-is-very-foolish-mistake/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1ZBNDg5NDE3MDMyMDI2UlAx and https://abcnews.com/amp/Politics/trump-blasts-nato-after-allies-rebuff-call-reopen/story?id=131113988

title: WikiLeaks: from 'I love' to 'I know nothing'

after.quote: I know nothing about WikiLeaks. It's not my thing.
after.where: Oval Office, White House, Washington, D.C.

context: Trump enthusiastically praised WikiLeaks during the 2016 campaign, then distanced himself from the organization following Julian Assange's arrest in 2019. The contrast is documented in contemporaneous reporting and an official presidential transcript.

title: NATO: 'obsolete' in 2016, 'no longer obsolete' in 2017

after.quote: I said it was obsolete. It's no longer obsolete.
after.where: White House joint press conference with NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg

context: Trump publicly reversed his characterization of NATO, citing changes in the alliance's focus on counterterrorism. This is an acknowledged policy assessment change, not necessarily evidence of deception.

title: Tax returns: 'it'll be released' versus continued refusal

before.quote: I don't mind releasing. I'm under a routine audit, and it'll be released.
before.where: First presidential debate, Hofstra University, Hempstead, New York

after.quote: I'm not releasing the tax returns because, as you know, they're under audit.
after.where: Press conference, Trump Tower, New York City

context: The 2016 statement suggested release after an audit; in 2017 Trump continued withholding the returns on audit grounds. An audit does not legally prevent voluntary publication. This is a change in stated willingness, not evidence of a legal obligation.

title: Abortion: punish women — then not women

before.quote: There has to be some form of punishment.
before.where: MSNBC town hall with Chris Matthews, Green Bay, Wisconsin

after.quote: The doctor or any other person performing this illegal act upon a woman would be held legally responsible, not the woman.
after.where: Written campaign statement issued after the town hall

context: In the town hall, Trump answered yes when pressed on punishment for women; later the same day, his campaign stated that women would not be punished. This is a same-day reversal, not a claim about current law.

title: Protester legal fees: a promise followed by a denial

before.quote: I promise you, I will pay for the legal fees. I promise. I promise.

after.quote: I never said I was going to pay for fees.

context: The earlier promise concerned a supporter confronting someone throwing tomatoes; the later statement denied having made a legal-fees promise. The original remarks and denial were compared by PolitiFact.

title: David Duke: denounced, then 'I don't know anything'

before.where: Press conference, Fort Worth, Texas, answering a question about David Duke

after.quote: I don't know anything about David Duke.
after.where: CNN State of the Union interview with Jake Tapper

context: Trump rejected Duke's endorsement two days before claiming unfamiliarity with him in a CNN interview. PolitiFact also documented earlier public comments about Duke.

title: Planned Parenthood: defund it, then keep some funding

after.quote: I'd look at the good aspects of it, and I would also look because I'm against abortion.

context: Trump first called for defunding Planned Parenthood, then discussed preserving support for its non-abortion health services. His position changed again in September. The precise distinction between funding the organization and specific services matters.
